metadata.note_on_EOU: EOU answer markings in source represent unconfirmed guesses. Correct answers here are determined independently from platform knowledge and source content.

questions.question: Which property controls how often a form displays to end users in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the Form Frequency property tells the form how often it should appear for users — for example, monthly, quarterly, or annually. A is incorrect — Form Requirement Level controls whether completing the form is required before advancing in the workflow, not how often it appears. B is incorrect — Form Type determines the kind of form (Cube View, Dashboard, or Spreadsheet), not its display frequency. D is incorrect — Profile Active controls whether the entire workflow profile is enabled or disabled, not the display frequency of individual forms.

questions.question: What must Cube Views, dashboards, and spreadsheets be added to in order to convert them into a form in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Cube Views, dashboards, and spreadsheets must be added to a Form Template to convert them into a form — the Form Template is the container that gives these objects their form behavior within a workflow. A is incorrect — Journals are used for recording manual adjustment entries, not for converting reporting objects into forms. B is incorrect — Dimensions define the structure of data in OneStream, not the mechanism for creating forms. D is incorrect — a Workflow Profile uses Form Templates by referencing them in workflow steps; the conversion to a form happens at the Form Template level, not directly in the Workflow Profile.

questions.question: How should an administrator disable a Base Input Workflow Profile in OneStream?

options.B: By switching the Profile Active setting to True
options.C: By switching the Profile Active setting to False
options.D: By deleting the Entity Assignment for that profile

questions.explanation: C is correct: switching the Profile Active setting to False will disable the Base Input Workflow Profile — the profile remains in place but is inactive, preserving its configuration for future use. A is incorrect — ignoring a profile in OnePlace does not disable it; it remains active and may still require user action. B is incorrect — setting Profile Active to True enables the profile; False is the setting used to disable it. D is incorrect — removing Entity Assignments changes which entities the profile applies to, but does not disable the profile itself.

questions.question: Which form type in OneStream has similar functionality to Excel?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the Spreadsheet form type has similar functionality to Excel — it allows users to work in a familiar spreadsheet-style interface with Excel-like formula and formatting capabilities. A is incorrect — Dashboards are interactive multi-component screens, not Excel-like spreadsheet environments. B is incorrect — Cube Views are grid-based reports for querying cube data; while grid-like, they do not replicate Excel's formula and cell manipulation functionality. D is incorrect — Journals are used for recording adjusting entries and do not replicate Excel functionality.

questions.question: Which right-click functionality in a Cube View can provide a detailed summary of the 18 members behind a cell of data?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Cell POV Information shows a detailed summary of the selected cell's 18 dimension members — it reveals exactly which member from each dimension contributes to that data intersection. A is incorrect — Cell Status shows the calculation status of the cell (such as OK, OK-MC, or Input Required) and whether it is locked, not the full 18-member breakdown. B is incorrect — 'Cell Detail' is not the standard name for this function; Cell POV Information is the correct term. C is incorrect — Drill Down shows the detail behind a cell's value and its audit history but does not display the full 18-member dimensional summary.

questions.question: Which right-click functionality in a Cube View allows a user to verify that a cell is available for data entry and view its audit history?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Drill Down shows whether the cell is available for data entry while also providing the ability to view the cell's audit history — it is the tool for investigating individual cell-level data provenance. A is incorrect — Cell Status shows the calculation state of a cell (locked, OK, Input Required, etc.) but does not provide the full audit history trail that Drill Down does. C is incorrect — Cell POV Information displays the 18 dimension members of the cell intersection but does not show audit history or data entry availability. D is incorrect — 'Cell Detail' is not a standard OneStream right-click option name.

questions.subtopic: Data Entry — Workflow Profile Types for Adjustments
questions.question: Which Workflow Profile Type is used to enter top-side adjustments to parent entities in OneStream?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Parent Input Profiles are specifically designed to enter top-side adjustments to parent entities — they allow adjustments through Forms or Adj input at the parent entity level rather than at the base entity level. A is incorrect — Review Profiles are used for reviewing, confirming, and certifying results from lower input profiles, not for entering data or adjustments. C is incorrect — Base Input Profiles collect data at the base entity level; top-side adjustments to parent entities are handled by Parent Input Profiles. D is incorrect — Data Adapters are components used in dashboards to retrieve and display data; they are not a Workflow Profile Type.

questions.question: Which option should be selected to see information about a cell, such as its amount, whether it is invalid, or whether it is locked?
questions.explanation: A is correct: Cell Status provides information about a cell including its amount, whether it is invalid, and whether it is locked — it gives the administrator or user a quick diagnostic view of the cell's current state. B is incorrect — Drill Down shows the detail data behind a cell and its audit history, but Cell Status is the specific option for viewing amount, validity, and lock status. C is incorrect — Cell POV Information shows the 18 dimension members of the intersection, not the cell's operational status such as lock state or validity. D is incorrect — Audit History is accessed through Drill Down, not as a separate top-level right-click option.

questions.subtopic: Data Entry — Manual Data Entry Form Types
questions.question: Which three form types can be used for manual data entry in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Cube Views, Dashboards, and Spreadsheets are the three form types that can be used for manual data entry in OneStream — each can be configured as a data entry form within a Form Template. A is incorrect — Journals are specialized tools for recording adjusting entries and are not one of the three primary form types for general manual data entry. B is incorrect — Journals are excluded from this set for the same reason; Dashboards, not Journals, complete the three primary form types. D is incorrect — this combination omits Cube Views, which are a core manual data entry form type.

questions.question: Which prefix is used in substitution variables to pull values from the Cube View POV?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the CV prefix is used in substitution variables to pull values from the Cube View POV — for example, !CV.Scenario! retrieves the current Scenario from the Cube View point-of-view context. A is incorrect — MF is not a standard substitution variable prefix used for Cube View POV values in OneStream. B is incorrect — WF is the prefix used for the Workflow POV (user's workflow context), not the Cube View POV. D is incorrect — POV is a general concept and not a substitution variable prefix; the specific prefix for Cube View context is CV.

questions.question: Which cells indicate that they are drillable in a OneStream Cube View?
questions.explanation: B is correct: blue cells in a Cube View indicate that the cell is drillable — users can double-click or drill into blue cells to see the detail data or lower-level breakdown behind the value. A is incorrect — red cells typically indicate a data error or invalid intersection, not drillable content. C is incorrect — green cells are not the standard indicator for drillable cells in OneStream. D is incorrect — gray cells typically indicate that a cell is locked or not available for data entry or drill, not that it is drillable.

questions.question: Which variable type is used to create dynamic headers, footers, and page captions in Cube Views?
questions.explanation: A is correct: Substitution Variables are used to create dynamic headers, footers, and page captions in Cube Views — they pull current POV values (such as the active Scenario, Time period, or Entity) into text elements, making the display context-aware and automatically updated. B is incorrect — Dimension Tokens (like E#, A#, S#) are used in Member Scripts and formulas to reference dimension members, not for creating dynamic display text in headers and captions. C is incorrect — Parameters are used to create interactive filters and selectors; while they can be dynamic, they are not specifically for headers, footers, and captions. D is incorrect — Expansion Variables are not a standard OneStream variable category; Substitution Variables are the correct type for dynamic text in report headers.

questions.question: What does the calculation status 'OK, MC' mean in OneStream?

options.A: Calculations are not required — no data exists for this intersection
options.B: The data for this intersection has not changed since the last calculation
options.C: The intersection was calculated but metadata has changed since the last calculation
options.D: The intersection is locked and cannot be recalculated

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'OK, MC' indicates the intersection was calculated but metadata has changed since the last calculation was run — the data may need to be recalculated to reflect the latest metadata structure. A is incorrect — when no data exists, the status would typically show as NoData or blank, not OK, MC. B is incorrect — data that has not changed since the last calculation would show a status of OK (without the MC suffix), indicating the calculation is current. D is incorrect — a locked intersection has its own lock indicator; OK, MC specifically signals metadata change, not a lock state.

questions.question: What step within a Workflow Profile can be configured to run a Calculation in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Calculations can be configured to run on the Process step within a Workflow Profile — the Calculation Definitions tab of the Process step is where Calc Types and Data Management Sequences are assigned. A is incorrect — the Validate step checks data for errors and rule compliance but does not run calculations. B is incorrect — the Confirm step is used to confirm that data has been reviewed and approved; it does not run calculations. D is incorrect — the Certify step is the final sign-off step and does not execute calculations.

questions.subtopic: Completing the Workflow — Cube View Calculations
questions.question: Where can calculation processes be enabled within a Cube View in OneStream?
questions.explanation: B is correct: setting the Can Calculate, Can Translate, and Can Consolidate properties to True in General settings > Common enables the user to perform these functions within the Cube View data explorer grid. A is incorrect — General settings > Report contains report formatting and layout properties, not calculation enablement settings. C is incorrect — General settings > Header Overrides is for customizing column and row headers, not for enabling calculation capabilities. D is incorrect — General settings > Security controls access permissions for the Cube View, not calculation process settings.

questions.subtopic: Completing the Workflow — Data Management in Workflow
questions.question: How can an administrator assign a Data Management job to a Workflow Profile?

options.A: On the Calculation Definitions tab of a Confirm workflow step, set Calc Type to No Calculate and populate the Filter field with the Data Management Sequence name
options.B: On the Calculation Definitions tab of a Validate workflow step, set Calc Type to No Calculate and populate the Filter field with the Data Management Sequence name
options.C: On the Calculation Definitions tab of a Process workflow step, set Calc Type to No Calculate and populate the Filter field with the Data Management Sequence name
options.D: On the Calculation Definitions tab of a Certify workflow step, set Calc Type to No Calculate and populate the Filter field with the Data Management Sequence name

questions.explanation: C is correct: within the Workflow on the Process step, a new Calculation Definition entry is added with the Calc Type set to No Calculate and the Filter field populated with the name of the Data Management Sequence to be executed. A is incorrect — the Confirm step is used for approval sign-off; Data Management Sequences are assigned through the Process step's Calculation Definitions, not Confirm. B is incorrect — the Validate step runs validation rules, not Data Management Sequences through Calculation Definitions. D is incorrect — the Certify step is the final certification action and does not support Data Management Sequence assignments through Calculation Definitions.

questions.question: What views can you work with using Task Scheduler in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Task Scheduler supports Calendar View and Grid View — Calendar View can be refined to show tasks by a range of timelines or groups, while Grid View lists the tasks and their properties in a tabular format. A is incorrect — Explorer Grid is not one of the Task Scheduler views; Grid View is the correct term. B is incorrect — Task View is not a named view in Task Scheduler; the two views are Calendar View and Grid View. D is incorrect — Workflow View is not a Task Scheduler view.

questions.subtopic: Completing the Workflow — Task Scheduler Frequency
questions.question: What is the minimum repeated time schedule that can be set within Task Scheduler in OneStream?
questions.explanation: D is correct: the minimum schedule interval in Task Scheduler is once every 5 minutes — this is the most frequent recurrence that can be configured for a scheduled task. A is incorrect — weekly is a valid schedule but it is the least frequent of the common intervals, not the minimum (most frequent). B is incorrect — daily scheduling is available but is far less frequent than the minimum 5-minute interval. C is incorrect — hourly is a common interval but the minimum supported frequency is every 5 minutes, which is more frequent.

questions.subtopic: Completing the Workflow — Confirmation Rule Status Colors
questions.question: What does a yellow status mean when a Confirmation Rule has been run in OneStream?

options.A: A rule has failed; the user cannot move on to the next task until it is resolved
options.B: A rule is presenting a warning, but the user can progress to the next task
options.D: A rule has not yet been run for this period

questions.explanation: B is correct: a yellow status on a Confirmation Rule means the rule is presenting a warning but the user can still progress to the next workflow task — it is a non-blocking alert. A is incorrect — a failed rule that prevents progression is indicated by a red status, not yellow. C is incorrect — a passed rule is indicated by a green status, not yellow. D is incorrect — a rule that has not been run would typically show no status or a neutral indicator, not yellow.

questions.subtopic: Completing the Workflow — Confirmation Rule Frequency
questions.question: What field within a Confirmation Rule defines the periods that it will run?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the Frequency field defines how often a Confirmation Rule will be used within a Workflow Profile — options include monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, yearly, or a custom time period set by a member filter. A is incorrect — the Order field determines the sequence in which confirmation rules are evaluated relative to each other, not the time periods in which they run. B is incorrect — the Action field defines what happens when the rule fires (warning vs. failure), not when it runs. D is incorrect — Rule Name is an identifier for the rule, not a time period control.

questions.subtopic: Completing the Workflow — Confirmation Profile Workflow Names
questions.question: Which Workflow Names would be valid when assigning a Confirmation Profile to a Workflow Profile?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Process, Confirm, and Certify are the valid Workflow Names for assigning a Confirmation Profile — a Confirm step always requires a Process step to occur ahead of it, so Process must be included in the valid set. A is incorrect — while Confirm and Certify are included, Process must also be present because a Confirm step cannot exist without a preceding Process step in the workflow. C is incorrect — Workspace is not a valid Workflow Name; it refers to a dashboard organizational structure, not a workflow step. D is incorrect — Validate is a step that runs before Process; it is not the correct starting Workflow Name for assigning Confirmation Profiles.

questions.subtopic: Completing the Workflow — Opening and Closing Workflows
questions.question: Where can a user close or open a Workflow Profile within OneStream?

options.A: Within a Parent Input Workflow Profile
options.B: Within a Base Input Workflow Profile
options.C: Within a Cube Root Workflow Profile

questions.explanation: C is correct: a user clicks the Close Workflow or Open Workflow button within the properties of the Cube Root Workflow Profile — this is the top-level control point for opening and closing the entire workflow hierarchy. A is incorrect — Parent Input Workflow Profiles control top-side adjustments for parent entities; they do not contain the Open/Close Workflow control. B is incorrect — Base Input Workflow Profiles are for base entity data collection; the workflow open/close function is at the Cube Root level. D is incorrect — the Default Workflow Profile is system-managed and used for status calculation; it does not contain workflow open/close controls.

questions.question: Where can certification questions be configured within OneStream?
questions.explanation: B is correct: certification questions are configured through Application > Workflow > Certification Questions — this is the administrative path within the workflow configuration area. A is incorrect — Data Sources contains configuration for data import sources, not certification questions. C is incorrect — Data Management contains data management sequences and steps, not certification question configuration. D is incorrect — the System tab is for system-level server administration, not application workflow configuration.

questions.subtopic: Finalizing Application Changes — Artifact Extract Format
questions.question: What primary file format is used for artifact extracts in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: application artifacts in OneStream are imported and exported using an XML format — this applies to metadata, Cube Views, dashboards, transformation rules, and other application components. A is incorrect — HTML is a presentation format for web content, not the format used for OneStream artifact extracts. B is incorrect — JSON is a data interchange format but is not the primary format used for OneStream application artifact extracts. D is incorrect — CSV is a tabular data format used for data imports; it is not the format for application artifact extracts such as metadata or configuration items.

questions.subtopic: Finalizing Application Changes — Dimension Comparison Utility
questions.question: What does a yellow row indicate within the Dimension Comparison Utility in OneStream?

options.B: At least one non-immediate descendant has been changed
options.C: The member's properties, or at least one immediate child, have been changed
options.D: The member has been added to the hierarchy

questions.explanation: B is correct: a yellow row in the Dimension Comparison Utility means at least one non-immediate descendant has been changed — the member itself and its immediate children are unchanged, but something deeper in its hierarchy branch has been modified. A is incorrect — a removed member is typically indicated by a red row or deletion marker, not yellow. C is incorrect — a member whose own properties or immediate children have changed is indicated by an orange row, not yellow; yellow specifically signals changes at a deeper descendant level. D is incorrect — a newly added member would be shown with a green row or addition marker, not yellow.
